summary: No restricted grammar: the one 'likely' flag ('Behalve') is a preposition in the bible's fixed punchline and both 'review' flags are tool errors. Two sentences would make a Dutch reader stumble: Petunia's wish rendered as plain indicative ('Ik wil dit van mijn man: hij luistert naar zijn vrouw') and the transitive 'studeer het maar'. The rest is small: an agentless 'Ze' opening b039, 'vertrok' in a sense the reader does not know, 'wedstrijd voor wiskunde', 'vertellen: dit zie ik', and 'excuus' where 'smoes' is the A2 word for the meaning.

findings.fragment: Ik wil, ik wil dit van mijn man: hij luistert naar zijn vrouw. Zij houdt van hem. En hij vertrouwt haar, deze ene keer—
findings.problem: After 'Ik wil dit van mijn man:' the indicative 'hij luistert' / 'hij vertrouwt haar' reads as a statement of fact, not a wish; 'En hij vertrouwt haar, deze ene keer' even asserts the opposite of what is happening, so the reader re-parses.
findings.evidence: EN: 'I want my husband to, to listen to his wife who loves him, and trust her just this once' (wish) vs NL present indicative after the colon; no modal, no imperative
findings.required_fix: Put the wish in a modal: 'Ik wil, ik wil dit van mijn man: hij moet naar zijn vrouw luisteren. Zij houdt van hem. En hij moet haar vertrouwen, deze ene keer—'. (Alternative without finite verbs: 'Ik wil, ik wil maar één ding van mijn man: luisteren naar zijn vrouw. Zij houdt van hem. En haar vertrouwen, deze ene keer—'.) Keep the stammer and the three short sentences.

findings.fragment: Dan stimuleerden ze hem altijd: studeer het maar.
findings.problem: 'studeren' does not take an object pronoun; 'studeer het maar' is not Dutch (one studies a subject, 'bestudeert' a thing).
findings.evidence: EN: 'encouraged to study whatever caught his attention'; lexicon: bestuderen known A2 ('to study, investigate')
findings.required_fix: 'Dan stimuleerden ze hem altijd: bestudeer het maar.' (or 'zoek het maar uit', uitzoeken A2).

findings.fragment: Ze behandelden hem goed, waarschijnlijk beter dan de meeste \gl{genetische}{genetic} vaders hun eigen kinderen.
findings.problem: The paragraph opens with 'Ze' right after a block in which only the Professor speaks; the reader has to supply 'his parents' before the gapped comparison ('… hun eigen kinderen [behandelden]') adds a second inference.
findings.evidence: EN agentless passive 'He was treated well'; NL active voice needs an agent and the antecedent is two blocks back
findings.required_fix: 'Zijn ouders behandelden hem goed, waarschijnlijk beter dan de meeste \gl{genetische}{genetic} vaders hun eigen kinderen.'

findings.problem: Good literary Dutch, but 'vertrekken' is in the reader's lexicon only as 'to leave' (A1); the sense 'twist (of a face)' is unknown and the sentence reads as nonsense to an A2 reader.
findings.evidence: lexicon vertrekken: known A1, en ['to leave']; the tool counts the token as known (polysemy false negative)
findings.required_fix: Either rephrase with known words: 'Harry trok een bitter gezicht.' — or keep and gloss the sense: 'Harry's mond \gl{vertrok}{twisted} bitter.' (b039 then has two glosses, the maximum).

findings.fragment: een wedstrijd voor wiskunde of wetenschap
findings.problem: 'een wedstrijd voor X' means a competition held for X's benefit; the preposition is copied from the English noun stack.
findings.evidence: EN: 'whatever maths or science competitions'; Dutch idiom is 'een wedstrijd in …' or a compound
findings.required_fix: 'Deed hij mee aan een wedstrijd in wiskunde of wetenschap?' (or 'een wiskunde- of wetenschapswedstrijd', compound of known parts).

findings.fragment: Je moet gewoon naar de wereld kijken en dan vertellen: dit zie ik.
findings.problem: 'vertellen' wants an addressee or a story; before a colon with direct content the natural verb is 'zeggen'.
findings.evidence: EN: 'report what you see'; indirect question avoided correctly, verb choice slightly off
findings.required_fix: 'Je moet gewoon naar de wereld kijken en dan zeggen: dit zie ik.'

findings.fragment: Dat leek een nogal verdacht soort excuus.
findings.problem: The reader knows 'excuus' as 'apology' (its only lexicon sense); the sense needed here is 'pretext', for which the A2 lexicon has 'smoes'.
findings.evidence: lexicon excuus: known A2, en ['apology']; smoes: known A2, en ['excuse', 'pretext']
findings.required_fix: 'Dat leek een nogal verdacht soort smoes.' (keep 'verdacht', A2 adjective).

findings.fragment: Toen kreeg hij eigen leraren uit de eindeloze voorraad arme studenten.
findings.problem: 'eigen leraren' is understandable but vague ('his own teachers' as opposed to whose?); Dutch says where the lesson happens.
findings.evidence: EN: 'he was provided with tutors'; privéleraar is B2, bijles (A2) implies remedial help
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Toen kreeg hij leraren aan huis, uit de eindeloze voorraad arme studenten.'

findings.fragment: haar hoofd kwam weer omhoog en ze staarde naar haar man
findings.problem: Literal rendering of 'her head rose back up'; readable, but 'opkijken' says it in one known verb.
findings.evidence: lexicon opkijken: known A2 ('to look up, to lift one's eyes')
findings.required_fix: Optional: '“Dank je, Harry. Maar—” ze keek weer op en staarde naar haar man.'

findings.fragment: keek op hem neer, afwijzend als altijd
findings.problem: 'op iemand neerkijken' is read first as figurative contempt; here that doubles 'afwijzend'. Natural Dutch, no stumble — recorded for the meaning reviewer, who decides whether the double reading is wanted.
findings.evidence: EN: 'looked down at him, dismissive as usual' (physical + attitude); b042 uses the physical 'keek omlaag naar hem' for the mother
findings.required_fix: No change required. If the physical reading is preferred: 'De Professor draaide zich om en keek omlaag naar hem, afwijzend als altijd.' 'afwijzend' needs no gloss (afwijzen A2).

findings.problem: English book title set in roman; the bible says English titles stay italic, the source block has no \emph.
findings.evidence: bible.md Naming policy: 'English book titles stay English and italic (Feynman Lectures …)' vs src b041 tex without \emph
findings.required_fix: Cohesion editor decides; if the bible wins: 'de \emph{Feynman Lectures on Physics}'.

findings.fragment: Een Doctor, docent biochemie in Oxford
findings.problem: Tool-unknown but transparent: 'Doctor' is the academic title, capitalised as Harry's sarcastic label in the source; 'biochemie' is in the cognate list.
findings.evidence: vocab row doctor: unknown, action review; src 'A Doctor teaching biochemistry at Oxford'
findings.required_fix: No change; do not gloss. Lexicon owner: add 'doctor' to exceptions.json → cognates.

findings.problem: Unknown lemma, glossed, half-transparent (cite / citation); fits Harry's register. b041 is at the gloss maximum (citaat, waarneming).
findings.evidence: vocab row citaat: unknown, glossed; gloss_per_paragraph_max 2
findings.required_fix: Keep. If a gloss slot is ever needed in b041, 'Daar staat ongeveer dit:' drops the word without loss.

findings.problem: Hard (B2) but it is Harry's fixed tic ('genetische ouders', bible) and a cognate; glossed once, recurs in s03.
findings.evidence: lexicon genetisch hard B2, glossed; bible.md Characters ch 1: verbal tic 'genetische ouders'
findings.required_fix: Keep as is. Cohesion editor: the gloss belongs to the first occurrence in the chapter (check s01).

findings.fragment: filosofen … je beslist dingen … Belangstelling Tonen (b039)
findings.problem: Stretch budget 4: 'filosoof' (B1) is a transparent cognate and fine unglossed; 'beslist' is the verb beslissen (A2), not the B1 adverb, so it does not count; 'Tonen' in the bible's capitalised phrase is the B1 verb the tool did not see. Budget used: 2 of 4.
findings.evidence: vocab rows filosoof ok-stretch, beslist ok-stretch (mis-tagged ADJ); lexicon tonen stretch B1; 'Belangstelling Tonen' counted as proper noun

flag_decisions.span: Behalve misschien een heel klein beetje
flag_decisions.reason: 'Behalve' is a preposition heading a verbless fragment ('Behalve misschien een heel klein beetje respect.'); there is no finite verb and no clause, so nothing is subordinated. The sentence is the bible's fixed punchline (Narrator voice §4).

'proberen te' is on exceptions.json grammar_whitelist (treat_as review). The alternatives ('wilde nadenken', 'ging nadenken') drop 'tried', which the next paragraph depends on; a single te-infinitive of a known verb in a 12-word sentence is accepted.
Plain attributive adjective ('een nogal verdacht soort excuus'); the lexicon lists 'verdacht' as ADJ A2 (suspicious). No participle phrase, no complements.

Reported at 0.2 (below ignore_confidence). Attributive adjective before 'kus', listed in the lexicon as ADJ A2 ('geruststellend'); restricted.md: simple adjectival participles in the lexicon are fine.

tool_feedback.ref: R-CONJ-OTHER likely 0.85 'Behalve misschien een heel klein beetje'
tool_feedback.reason: 'behalve' is a preposition unless followed by 'dat'/'als' or a finite verb; the rule should require a clause (finite verb after the word) before firing. Verbless fragments should never produce a conjunction flag.
Both words have an ADJ entry in the lexicon and stand alone before a noun; a participle used attributively, without complements, and listed as ADJ should not be flagged.

'je beslist dingen met een experiment' is 2sg present of beslissen (A2); forms table already maps beslist → beslissen. When a token has a subject pronoun before it, prefer the verb reading over the adverb/adjective entry.

Capitalised bible phrases are counted as proper nouns, so the B1 verb 'tonen' never appears in the table; lowercase 'tonen' would also be lemmatised to the noun 'toon'. Capitalised mid-sentence words that exist in the lexicon should be looked up before being treated as names.

Both lemmas are known A1/A2, but in senses the reader has not learned ('vertrekken' = twist of a face; 'excuus' = pretext). Not fixable by lemma status; worth a 'sense' field on the few frequent polysemous verbs, or a reviewer checklist entry.
Transparent title cognate; add 'doctor' to exceptions.json → cognates.
Absent from every list; likely B1. Add with en 'quote, quotation' so it stops surfacing as unknown.
